flashcards.q: What single question does each of the four gates answer?
flashcards.a: POC: can this be built at all? Prototype: is this the right thing to build? MVP: will real users adopt this at small scale? Production: will it hold up under real load/failure/cost/ops indefinitely?

flashcards.q: What did RAND's 2025 analysis find about AI project failure, broken down?
flashcards.a: 80.3% of AI projects fail to deliver intended business value: 33.8% abandoned before reaching production, 28.4% complete but underdeliver, 18.1% deliver some value but can't justify cost.

flashcards.q: What did the March 2026 survey of 650 enterprise tech leaders find about AI agent pilots?
flashcards.a: 78% of enterprises have AI agent pilots running, but only 14% have successfully scaled an agent to organization-wide operational use.

flashcards.q: Per multiple 2026 analyses, what's the primary cause of AI pilots failing to reach production â€” model capability or something else?
flashcards.a: Organizational/operational causes: data readiness gaps, unclear ownership, missing evaluation infrastructure, and change management debt â€” not model capability.

flashcards.q: What is a 'Wizard of Oz' prototype and what's its biggest planning risk?
flashcards.a: A prototype where a human manually performs the function the system would eventually automate, behind a real-looking interface. Risk: the human can silently handle edge cases/quality the real automated system can't match, so a successful test validates the concept, not the real system's achievable quality.

flashcards.q: What is the AI-specific addition to the classic MVP-to-production gate that traditional CRUD features don't need?
flashcards.a: An automated evaluation harness (golden set with known-good outputs or a graded rubric) gating every model/prompt/retrieval-config change, plus drift monitoring on live traffic â€” because output quality can silently degrade in ways a binary-correctness test suite wouldn't catch.

flashcards.q: Name five concrete dimensions that structurally change between MVP and production (not just 'more polish').
flashcards.a: Scale (load-tested vs. informal), failure handling (full resilience catalogue vs. errors surface), observability (traces/alerts/on-call vs. basic logs), cost (modeled and owned vs. tracked roughly), rollback (automated/staged vs. manual ad hoc).

flashcards.q: What's the single most expensive mistake in the POC-to-prod pipeline?
flashcards.a: Skipping a gate's QUESTION while reusing its CODE â€” e.g. taking POC code straight to production because 'it already works,' inheriting all the risk the POC deliberately never tested.

flashcards.q: What makes a valid gate exit criterion versus an invalid one?
flashcards.a: Valid: specific, measured, observed outcome ('6/8 users completed the task unaided'). Invalid: a vague impression or internal approval ('the demo went well').

flashcards.q: Why can an MVP pilot succeed on its cohort but fail at full production rollout?
flashcards.a: Pilot cohorts are often self-selected (early adopters, more tolerant, sometimes internal/friendly users) and don't represent the full population's needs or usage patterns â€” MVP exit criteria measured on a non-representative cohort can mask a mismatch that only appears at real scale.

flashcards.q: What did MIT-associated research find about the P&L impact of enterprise AI pilots?
flashcards.a: Roughly 95% of enterprise AI pilots deliver zero measurable P&L impact.

flashcards.q: How should you give leadership a project cost estimate without hiding the staged-gate structure inside one number?
flashcards.a: Give a firm number for the next gate only, plus a conditional range for what follows based on that gate's outcome, and name the abandonment branch explicitly â€” one collapsed total either overstates near-term spend or hides the real chance the project stops before production.

flashcards.q: Production reveals the MVP's core adoption assumption was wrong for the general population. What's the correct move?
flashcards.a: Treat it as the prototype gate's question (is this the right thing to build) failing retroactively, and re-run real user validation with a representative sample â€” not push forward with production hardening, which fixes an operational problem, not a product-fit one.
